subject.title: Token-gated dashboard snapshots for codexbar serve (restart of #1026)

question: Should CodexBar officially support direct non-loopback plain-HTTP serving when a static bearer token and explicit `--allow-plain-http` acknowledgment are supplied?
rationale: The implementation deliberately permits a replayable credential and account data to cross a network without transport encryption; tests can verify mechanics, but only maintainers can accept that permanent product security boundary.

options.title: Accept Trusted-Network Mode
options.body: Accept the documented opt-in plain-HTTP mode while preserving loopback defaults, full data-route authentication, and prominent TLS reverse-proxy guidance.

options.title: Require Encrypted Transport
options.body: Remove direct non-loopback plain HTTP and require users to expose the loopback service through a TLS-terminating proxy or future native TLS support.

options.title: Keep Serve Loopback-Only
options.body: Decline remote serving for now and limit the snapshot endpoint to authenticated loopback clients.

recommendation.title: Accept Trusted-Network Mode
recommendation.body: Accept the documented opt-in plain-HTTP mode while preserving loopback defaults, full data-route authentication, and prominent TLS reverse-proxy guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: The original serve behavior and the earlier dashboard discussion indicate this person is the best available owner for the product and security boundary.
